content.Title: 2021 ACC/AHA/SCAI Coronary Revascularization Guideline
content.Focus: The guideline provides information on coronary revascularization techniques, especially comparing off-pump and on-pump coronary artery bypass grafting. It also discusses strategies for reducing sternal wound infections and the effects of different perioperative management approaches in cardiac surgeries.
Key Topics: Comparison between off-pump and on-pump coronary artery bypass outcomes
Importance of complete revascularization to reduce complications
Postoperative management strategies, including insulin infusion for reducing sternal wound infections
Details from various studies on different surgical approaches and patient outcomes in coronary surgeries

Studies Mentioned.Study: Danish On-pump Versus Off-pump Randomization Study (DOORS)
Studies Mentioned.Findings: Off-pump coronary artery bypass surgery is inferior in graft patency compared to on-pump surgeries.
Off-pump coronary artery bypass provides benefits such as reduced myocardial injury and transfusion requirements.

Studies Mentioned.Finding: Five-year quality of life between off-pump and on-pump coronary surgeries has been evaluated.

Studies Mentioned.Authors: Lazar HL, Chipkin SR, et al.
Studies Mentioned.Findings: Tight glucose control during coronary artery bypass decreases ischemic events

content.Focus Area: Insulin infusion and other methods to reduce sternal wound infection in CABG patients, and the impact of perioperative management strategies on patient outcomes.
